description: Detailed (ground-truth) game rules used as a reference to evaluate whether the AI player extracted rules from the VIDEO that are NOT mentioned in the standard game_rules.json. To be filled per game over time; empty string means 'not yet curated' (analysis should fall back to skipping that game).

games.Taxi-v3:
You need to move the taxi to the passenger’s square first and perform the pickup action. Then move the taxi to the colorful square in front of the building and perform the dropoff action to clear the level. 
View: a 2D top-down pixel view. You see a yellow taxi moving in a road maze, with colored pickup/dropoff locations marked by red, green, yellow, and blue zones, and hedges forming the walls and obstacles.
You may not move onto any square occupied by a flower bed. Performing pickup or dropoff in the wrong location will cause the game to fail immediately.
Scoring rule: Each step costs -1 except drop-off. Successful drop-off: +20
Strategy: Navigate to the passenger, pick up, navigate to destination, drop off. Avoid illegal actions.
games.CliffWalking-v1:
Game Description
This is a 2D side-scrolling navigation game where the player controls a character across a linear, grid-based platform. The environment consists of a grassy upper layer and a brown earthen foundation. The objective is to navigate from the starting point to get the pancake on the far right.
Game Mechanics and Rules
- Movement: The character moves in discrete steps. 
- Victory Condition: To win the game, the player must reach pancake on the far right.
- Failure Condition: The platform is bordered by a cliff. Falling off the cliff at any point results in an immediate failure and ends the game.
Guidance for Success
1. Traverse the Platform: Begin by moviroadng steadily to the right. Precision is key; ensure the character remains on the grassy surface.
games.CartPole-v1:
A pole is attached to a cart that moves along a frictionless track.
You control a cart that slides along a frictionless one-dimensional track, with an unactuated pole hinged at its top. Your objective is to control the cart by pushing it left or right to keep the pole balanced upright for as long as possible.
View: a 2D side view rendered as pixels. You see the cart as a horizontal block on a track, and the pole as a thin rod attached to a pivot on the cart's top.
Action space: Discrete(2). 0 = apply a fixed leftward force to the cart, 1 = apply a fixed rightward force to the cart. There is no zero/no-op action; you must push every step.The force magnitude is fixed.
Termination conditions: The episode terminates as soon as any of the following conditions becomes true: the pole angle exceeds ±12 degrees from vertical, about ±0.2095 radians; or the cart position exceeds ±2.4 units along the track.
Scoring rule: Gain 2 points for each survival step.
Strategy 1: Push the cart in the direction the pole is falling to counterbalance it.
Strategy 2: The cart has inertia, so you need to act in advance by pushing in the opposite direction of the cart’s current movement to prevent it from moving too far in one direction.
Strategy 3: Keep the cart near the center of the screen so you have enough space to recover in either direction.
games.Acrobot-v1:
Game Description
This is a physics-based "Acrobot" simulation game. The player controls a two-link robotic arm (consisting of two teal segments and two yellow joints). The top joint is pinned to a fixed point in space, while the middle joint is actuated. The game takes place in a gravity-affected environment.
Core Mechanics & Rules
- The Arm: The system consists of two links. The first link is attached to a pivot, and the second link is attached to the end of the first.
- Controls (Torque): The player can apply rotational force (torque) to the middle joint.
  - Torque +1: Applies force in one rotational direction.
  - Torque -1: Applies force in the opposite rotational direction.
- Objective: The goal is to swing the tip of the second (lower) link high enough to touch or cross the horizontal black line located near the top of the screen.
- Victory Condition: Once any part of the lower segment crosses the target line, the "Victory" state is achieved.
Guidance & Strategy
To succeed in this game, you must understand the principle of momentum and oscillation. Because the motor in the middle joint is typically not strong enough to lift the arm straight up from a dead stop, you must "pump" the swing.
1. Build Momentum: Start by applying torque in one direction (e.g., +1). As the arm begins to swing and reaches its highest point on one side, reverse the torque (e.g., -1) to accelerate it as it falls back down.
2. Manage the Center of Mass: Use the middle joint to tuck or extend the lower link. Tucking the link in as it moves toward the center and extending it as it moves away can help increase the swing's amplitude.
3. The Final Push: As the swings become wider, the arm will eventually gain enough velocity to flip over the top pivot. Continue applying consistent torque until the lower tip breaks the plane of the black line to trigger the victory.
games.ALE/Enduro-v5:
Your goal is to pass as many cars as possible.
View: Third-person, behind your car. The road curves left and right, scenery such as mountains, trees, palm trees, and snow appears in the distance and rolls past as you accelerate, and other vehicles move in front of you.
Visible elements: Your race car at the bottom of the screen; opponent cars ahead of you, and rarely behind you in the same lane; the road and its curving shoulders; distant scenery that changes with time of day and weather; and a HUD at the bottom showing the current day number and a 'cars-to-go' counter that decreases each time you successfully pass a car.
Colliding with other cars or scraping against the edge of the track will cause your car to slow down.
Scoring rule: Gain 1 point for overtaking; lose 1 point when being overtaken.
Strategy 1: When your car is moving fast and another car suddenly appears directly ahead, slowing down and steering at the same time can effectively help you avoid a collision. 
Strategy 2: Stay on full accelerator whenever the road is dry and clear.
games.ALE/Freeway-v5:
Game Description
This is a retro-style arcade game where the player controls a small yellow chicken—positioned at the bottom of a multi-lane highway.
Core Mechanics & Rules:
- The Environment: The play area consists of multiple horizontal lanes. Cars of various colors (red, blue, green, yellow, etc.) move across these lanes at different, constant speeds.
- Controls:
  - Up: Moves the character forward toward the goal.
  - Down: Moves the character backward toward the starting line.
  - NOOP (No Operation): The character stands still, which is essential for timing gaps in traffic.
- Collision Penalty: If the character is hit by a car, they are either pushed back to a lower lane or sent entirely back to the starting point (depending on the specific game version). This resets progress and forces the player to re-navigate the road.
- Victory Condition: Reaching the top-most gray area above the final lane triggers the "Victory" state.
Guidance & Strategy
Follow these strategic tips to reach the finish line:
1. Prioritize Timing over Speed: Moving "Up" constantly will almost certainly result in a collision. The game is a test of patience.
2. Utilize the "NOOP" Action: Watch the flow of traffic and wait for a "window" of clear space before advancing to the next lane.
3. Watch for High-Speed Vehicles: Some cars move significantly faster than others. If a fast car is approaching and you cannot clear the lane in time, use the Down action to retreat to a safer position rather than taking the hit.
games.ALE/Seaquest-v5: Atari Seaquest: Pilot a submarine to rescue stranded divers and eliminate underwater enemies. Perspective: Side view of an ocean profile. The surface (you can surface) is at the top of the screen; players can move left, right, up, and down in the water below the surface (using combination keys). Objective: Rescue divers and shoot enemies to earn points; survive as long as possible. There is no clear end screen (unless you die); the goal is to get the highest score. Visible Elements: Your submarine (the player character, capable of firing horizontal torpedoes in the direction you are currently facing); Killer sharks (swimming horizontally, they will eat you if they touch you); Enemy submarines (swimming horizontally, white submarines will fire their own bullets); Divers (small humanoid characters floating horizontally with their arms raised; touch them to rescue); A horizontal oxygen bar near the top of the screen; diving does not consume oxygen (the game mechanics have been specially modified); A row of small diver icons near the score, showing the number of divers currently on your submarine (maximum 6); Current score. Controls: Move the submarine up, down, left, and right; fire torpedoes in the current direction. Diagonal movement is also effective (submarine diagonal movement), and torpedo firing can be done simultaneously with movement. There is no dedicated "surface" button—surface by moving upwards to the surface line. Scoring: Killing an enemy +20 points, contacting a diver +30 points, and each diver provides +50 points upon surfacing. Death: If (a) an enemy touches you, (b) a white submarine enemy torpedoes you, or (c) you surface without any rescued divers on board. Game Progression: There are no separate waves. Hidden/Inconspicuous Mechanics: The oxygen bar is unlimited in this version of the game; scores are tracked by memory and are not displayed as actual scores. The maximum number of divers a player can carry is six; a seventh diver cannot be collected until the count is reset upon surfacing. Surfacing too early (with only one or two divers) is wasteful. Strategy: Collect as many divers as possible, but allow enough time before the maximum number of steps is cut off, otherwise you will lose the maximum bonus points for surfacing after reaching the step limit; actively attack enemies before they collide with you or fire bullets at you; remember the direction in which enemies swim to avoid bumping into them while moving.
games.ALE/Pong-v5:
Your objective is to control the paddle to hit the ball.
Visible elements: Your paddle, on the right side of the screen by default, is a short vertical bar that can move only up and down. The CPU opponent paddle is on the left side and is also a vertical bar. A square ball bounces between the paddles and off the top and bottom walls. There is a horizontal mid-court dashed line, and two single-digit or two-digit numeric score readouts at the top of the screen, one for each player.
Controls: Up and Down move your paddle vertically.
Ball physics: The paddle is internally divided into segments. Where the ball strikes the paddle determines the return angle. A center hit returns the ball nearly perpendicular, while edge hits produce steeper angles. The ball speeds up the longer a rally lasts and resets to a slow speed whenever a point is scored.
Scoring rule: Gain 1 point for catching the ball; lose 1 point for dropping/missing the ball.
You control the right paddle; the AI opponent controls the left.
After either side misses, the game resets and the ball serves from the center.
games.CustomBreakout:
Game Description
This is a classic arcade-style block-breaking game. The game features a player-controlled paddle at the bottom of the screen, a bouncing ball, and a series of target bricks at the top. The visual interface tracks the current Score and the number of Lives remaining.
Core Mechanics & Rules
- Scoring: Every time the ball strikes and destroys a brick, the score increases.
- Movement & Control:
  - Left/Right: The paddle can be moved horizontally across the bottom of the screen to intercept the ball.
  - NOOP (Neutral): The paddle remains stationary.
  - Fire: The paddle launches the ball.
- Physics: The ball bounces off the paddle, the side walls, and the bricks. The angle at which the ball hits the paddle determines its trajectory back toward the bricks.
- Failure Condition: The player must not let the ball pass the paddle. Missing the ball as it bounces back toward the bottom results in an immediate failure and ends the game.
- Victory Condition: The game is won when the target bricks are successfully cleared.
Guidance & Strategy
To achieve "Victory" and maximize your score, follow these strategic guidelines:
1. Anticipate the Trajectory: Do not wait for the ball to reach the bottom. Watch the angle at which the ball hits the top bricks or side walls to predict where it will land, and move the paddle to that position in advance.
2. Stay Alert on the Rebound: The ball’s speed or angle may change slightly after hitting a brick. Always stay focused on the "return trip" to avoid the failure condition of missing the ball.
games.MountainCar-v0:
Game Description
This is a physics-based challenge. The player controls a small black car positioned in a deep valley between two hills.
Core Mechanics & Rules
- The Environment: The track is a sinusoidal curve. Gravity is the primary force acting against the car.
- The Constraint (Underpowered Engine): The car’s engine is not strong enough to climb the right-hand hill from a standing start or by simply holding the "Accelerate Right" button.
- Controls:
  - Accelerate Left: Applies force to move the car toward the left hill.
  - Accelerate Right: Applies force to move the car toward the right hill (the goal).
- Victory Condition: The game is won when the car's position reaches or passes the yellow flag at the top of the right-hand slope.
Guidance & Strategy: Building Momentum
To win this game, you must use the physics of momentum (potential and kinetic energy). Simply driving toward the goal will result in the car stalling and sliding back down. Follow this "swing" strategy demonstrated in the video:
1. The Gravity Assist: Once the car reaches its peak and begins to slide back down, switch your input.
2. Build Potential Energy: If you can't reach the top in one swing, repeat the process—rocking back and forth higher each time—until you have enough speed to reach the peak.
games.CustomLavaCrossing-v0: This is a MiniGrid lava crossing puzzle on an nxn walled grid. Objective: Reach the green target block in the bottom right corner of the room while avoiding the deadly orange lava blocks. View: A top-down 2D grid. The agent is a red triangle with its vertices pointing in the direction it is currently facing. By default, the underlying MiniGrid environment is partially observable—the agent only receives an n*n egocentric view of the blocks in front of it—this benchmark only renders the portion of the grid in front of the agent for human/AI viewing. Inference must take into account the agent's facing direction. Visible elements: The red triangle agent, the gray walls forming the outer boundary, the horizontal or vertical orange lava bands spanning the grid, and the green target block. There are no keys, doors, or pick-up items in this environment. Action Space (MiniGrid Standard, 7 Discrete Actions): 0 = Turn Left (rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise in place), 1 = Turn Right (rotate 90 degrees clockwise in place), 2 = Move Forward (move one cell in the facing direction), 3 = Pick Up, 4 = Drop, 5 = Toggle, 6 = Complete. In this environment, only actions 0, 1, and 2 are meaningful—no items need to be picked up, dropped, toggled, or completed. Layout: The agent is generated in the top-left inner corner (cell (1,1)), facing right, with the target located in the bottom-right inner corner (cell (9,9)). N=5 lava rivers traverse the grid; each lava river is either perfectly horizontal or perfectly vertical, and each lava river has exactly one safe crossing cell. The generator guarantees that the path from the start to the end point can pass through these 5 crossings. Score: The agent earns (steps of shortest_path / step_count) points upon reaching the objective; 0 points are awarded for stepping into lava or running out of time. Termination/Truncation: The game round ends immediately if the agent steps into a lava tile (death) or reaches a green objective (success). Rounds are truncated when the maximum number of steps is exceeded. This benchmark limits rounds to 40 steps – exceeding 40 steps results in game failure. Hidden Mechanics: Hitting a wall forward has no effect (the agent remains stationary but still consumes a step); stepping into lava is fatal; turning around also consumes a step, so simple "spinning and looking around" wastes steps; the agent cannot slide diagonally across a river – it must precisely step onto a safe crossing point. Strategy: Safe paths within the visible area are largely deterministic. While there are forks in the road, most are dead ends, as can be seen from history frames. Avoid them. Simply following the safe path and avoiding backtracking will generally lead to the optimal solution.
games.CustomMultiRoom-v0: This is a MiniGrid multi-room navigation puzzle on an nxn walled grid (the outer grid size varies by difficulty) containing 6 connected rooms. Objective: Walk through the chain of 6 connected rooms and reach the green goal square in the final room. View: A top-down 2D grid. The agent is a red triangle with its vertices pointing in the direction it is currently facing. By default, the underlying MiniGrid environment is partially observable—the agent only receives an egocentric view of the cells in front of it—this benchmark only renders the portion of the grid in front of the agent for human/AI viewing. Inference must take into account the agent's facing direction. Visible elements: The red triangle agent, the gray walls outlining each room and the outer boundary, 5 colored doors connecting consecutive rooms, and the goal square in the last room. Door colors rotate so that doors within the same room are visually distinct. There are no keys, locked doors, lava, or pick-up items in this environment. Action Space (MiniGrid Standard, 7 Discrete Actions): 0 = Turn Left (rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise in place), 1 = Turn Right (rotate 90 degrees clockwise in place), 2 = Move Forward (move one cell in the facing direction), 3 = Pick Up, 4 = Drop, 5 = Toggle, 6 = Complete. In this environment, only actions 0, 1, 2, and 5 are meaningful—Toggle (5) opens or closes a door directly in front of the agent, while Pick Up, Drop, and Complete do nothing. Layout: The outer grid holds 6 procedurally placed connected rooms, each up to 10x10. Consecutive rooms share exactly one wall tile that is a colored door, for 5 doors total. Room shapes and positions are randomized every episode. Score: The ratio of opened doors to total doors accounts for 50 points out of a full score of 100, and another 50 points out of 100 are awarded based on path efficiency calculated as shortest_path / step_count after reaching the destination. Termination/Truncation: The game round ends immediately when the agent steps onto the goal square (success). Rounds are truncated when the maximum number of steps is exceeded. This benchmark limits rounds to 70 steps – exceeding 70 steps results in game failure. Hidden Mechanics: Doors start closed but unlocked; walking forward into a closed door does nothing and still consumes a step—the agent must face the door and use Toggle (5) to open it first, after which it can be walked through (toggling again would close it). Because the true observation is only an area in front, when entering a new room the agent may need to turn to scan for the next door. Hitting a wall forward has no effect but still consumes a step. Pick Up and Drop have no effect—there is nothing to pick up. Strategy: Traverse the rooms in sequence, open each door the instant you are facing it, and minimize turns. With only 70 steps for up to 6 rooms there is essentially no slack for backtracking—plan the room order from the visible layout, commit to it, and you will generally get the optimal solution.
games.CustomUnlockPickup-v0: This is a MiniGrid unlock-and-pickup puzzle on a walled grid split into two side-by-side rooms (each room's size varies by difficulty). The mission is 'pick up the {color} box', where the color is randomized each episode. Objective: Pick up the key in the left room, use it to unlock and open the locked door between the two rooms, enter the right room, and pick up the colored target box. View: A top-down 2D grid. The agent is a red triangle with its vertices pointing in the direction it is currently facing. By default, the underlying MiniGrid environment is partially observable—the agent only receives a 7x7 egocentric view of the cells in front of it—this benchmark only renders the portion of the grid in front of the agent for human/AI viewing. Inference must take into account the agent's facing direction. Visible elements: The red triangle agent, the gray walls including the vertical interior wall that separates the two rooms, one colored key lying on the floor of the left room, one colored locked door set into the interior wall, and one colored target box in the right room. The key color always matches the door color; both are randomized per episode. Action Space (MiniGrid Standard, 7 Discrete Actions): 0 = Turn Left (rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise in place), 1 = Turn Right (rotate 90 degrees clockwise in place), 2 = Move Forward (move one cell in the facing direction), 3 = Pick Up, 4 = Drop, 5 = Toggle, 6 = Complete. In this environment, actions 0 through 5 may all be needed—Complete (6) is not required. Layout: 1 row by 2 columns of rooms (room size varies by difficulty, typically 7 to 11 tiles per side) joined by a shared vertical interior wall. The agent and the key spawn in the left room; the locked door sits in the vertical interior wall; the target box sits in the right room. Score: The task comprises four ordered milestones: picking up the key, opening the door, dropping the key to free up hands for picking up items, and picking up the item. The first 3 milestones are worth 20 points each, and the last one is worth 40 points. Failing to pick up the item results in just a failing grade. Termination/Truncation: The game round ends immediately when the agent finishes a step carrying the target box (success). Rounds are truncated when the maximum number of steps is exceeded. This benchmark limits rounds to 40 steps – exceeding 40 steps results in game failure. Hidden Mechanics: The agent can carry only one object at a time, so it must drop the key before it can pick up the box. Pick Up (3) acts only on the tile directly in front of the agent—you cannot pick up an item by standing on it. The agent cannot walk over the key on the floor; it must either pick the key up or detour around it (project-specific wrapper behavior). Drop (4) places the carried key onto the empty floor tile directly in front, and a project-specific restriction rejects any attempt to drop the key onto the door tile, whether that door is open or closed. Toggle (5) unlocks and opens a locked door when the agent is carrying the matching-color key. Walking forward into a closed or locked door is blocked and just wastes a step. Strategy: Orient toward the key and pick it up; navigate to the door and Toggle to unlock and open it; step into the right room; find an empty floor tile next to you that is NOT the door tile, face it, and drop the key; then orient toward the box and pick it up. Minimize turns—every turn costs one of your 40 steps.
games.ALE/Frostbite-v5: Atari Frostbite: Jump between ice floes to collect ice blocks. View: Side view. The top third of the screen shows a snowy shore where igloos are being built; the bottom two-thirds is open water with four rows of horizontally arranged ice floes rolling left and right (adjacent rows roll in opposite directions). Obstacles will move or walk on the ice floes. Objective: Collect ice blocks by jumping onto white ice floes; when you jump onto a layer, the ice blocks on that layer turn blue and become uncollectible. Visible elements: Frostbite Bailey (player character, an Inuit, starts from the shore and jumps between ice floes); four rows of ice floes, each consisting of four ice blocks (some ice blocks may be off-screen); igloos being built on the shore (the igloos grow larger as you collect ice blocks); snow geese/snowbirds occasionally appear (flying along a row of ice floes, contact is fatal); Controls: Jump up to the next row of ice floes closer to the shore; jump down to the next row of ice floes further away from the shore. Move left and right to move laterally along Bailey's current ice floe. Scoring Rules (from the manual): Each white ice floe Bailey lands on counts as an igloo block and earns points. Survival: At the start of the game, you have one active Bailey character and three spare lives. You will lose a life if you: (a) fall into the water (miss an ice floe), (b) Touching any hazards. Hidden/Non-obvious mechanics: Jumping onto a white ice floe turns its entire row blue and adds a block to the igloo; jumping onto a blue ice floe does not reduce blocks or score points. When all ice floes turn blue, the row resets to white and can be collected again. When you jump to the last layer of ice, all ice blocks, including the last layer, reset to white. You must jump up and then down to the last layer to collect the ice blocks after the reset. Strategy: First, observe the direction of ice block movement to avoid jumping and falling into the water; avoid moving too far between jumps; use key combinations efficiently; Bonus points: Collecting ice blocks alone earns bonus points, and death may incur penalties.
games.ALE/BeamRider-v5:
Atari Beamrider: fly along the front face of a 3D grid (the Restrictor Shield) shooting alien craft sector by sector.
View: pseudo-3D, looking forward down a tunnel. The screen shows a grid of beams converging toward a vanishing point at the top; five vertical beams reach down to the bottom where your ship sits, with horizontal cross-beams perceived as receding into the distance.
Objective: clear the 99 sectors of the Restrictor Shield. To clear one sector you must destroy 15 enemy saucers, then defeat the Sector Sentinel that appears.
Visible elements: your Beamrider ship at the bottom of the screen, which can only sit on one of the five vertical beams; enemy craft that ride along beams or fly across them; the Sector Sentinel, a large mothership that cruises across the top after the 15 saucers are gone; HUD showing the current sector number, score, number of reserve ships, and number of torpedoes remaining (3 per sector).
Controls: Left and Right snap the ship from the current vertical beam to the adjacent one (you cannot float between beams); Fire shoots a short-range laser straight up the current beam; a separate input fires a torpedo (up to 3 per sector) which travels up the beam and destroys the first object it hits including the Sector Sentinel. There is no vertical motion of the ship.
Enemy roster by sector of first appearance (Atari 2600 version): sector 1 white saucers (the standard target, killable by laser); sector 2 brown space debris (not killable, must be dodged); sector 4 yellow chirper ships (killable, fast); sector 6 green blocker ships (cannot be lased, only torpedoed or dodged); sector 8 green bounce craft (cannot be lased); sector 10 blue chargers (killable); sector 12 orange trackers (cannot be lased, home in on you); sector 16 magnetic mines (cannot be lased). Yellow Rejuvenators that look like miniatures of your own ship occasionally drift down a beam: collecting one grants an extra life, but shooting one turns it into lethal debris.
Scoring rules: points are awarded per enemy destroyed and increase with the sector number; the Sector Sentinel grants a sizable bonus, with an extra multiplier applied per reserve ship still in your fleet. The manual does not publish per-enemy point values but explicitly states they scale with sector. Only the 15 white saucers count toward sector progress; killing other enemy types is optional scoring.
Lives / death: start with multiple reserve ships displayed on the right of the HUD. You lose a ship if (a) any non-rejuvenator enemy touches your ship, (b) you collide with debris, (c) a homing tracker reaches your beam, (d) you shoot a rejuvenator and the resulting debris reaches you. Running out of reserves ends the game.
Progression: a new enemy type is added every other sector up through sector 16, then patterns recombine at increasing speed. Torpedoes refresh to 3 at the start of every new sector - unused torpedoes do NOT carry over.
Hidden / non-obvious mechanics: the ship is locked to discrete vertical beams - this is a five-position lateral game, not a free-motion shooter; the laser is short range and can be out-distanced by enemies at the top of the grid; only torpedoes hurt the Sector Sentinel; rejuvenators look so similar to your ship that they are commonly shot by accident.
Strategy: bank the 15 saucers as fast as possible while saving at least one torpedo for the Sentinel; do not fire on anything that resembles a rejuvenator until you are certain; use lateral snaps to dodge homing trackers; when a beam is blocked by a non-killable green blocker, snap sideways rather than waste shots.
Reward signal in Gym: per-step delta of the raw Atari score (saucer kills + sentinel bonus + optional extra-enemy points). No custom shaping is applied in the default ALE/BeamRider-v5 wrapper.
games.ALE/Assault-v5:
Game Description
This is a retro-style fixed-shooter arcade game. The player controls a small spaceship at the bottom of the screen, tasked with defending space against waves of alien invaders and a large command ship (mothership) at the top.
Core Mechanics & Rules
- The Player: You control a starship that moves horizontally along a fixed line at the bottom of the screen.
- The Enemies:
  - Invaders: Smaller, crab-like aliens that move in patterns and descend toward the player.
  - Mothership: A large, multi-colored craft at the top of the screen that acts as a primary target.
- Controls:
  - Left / Right: Moves the ship horizontally to aim at enemies or dodge incoming fire.
  - Up: Fires a vertical laser projectile toward the top of the screen.
  - NOOP (No Operation): The ship stays in its current position, allowing for careful timing.
- Scoring: Every enemy destroyed adds points to the score counter at the top of the screen.
- Failure Condition (Critical Rule): You must avoid the enemy projectiles. Getting hit by a single enemy projectile leads to immediate failure and ends the game.
- Victory Condition: Destroying 3 invaders triggers the Victory state.
Step-by-Step Guidance
To achieve victory as shown in the gameplay sequence, follow these strategies:
1. Prioritize Movement and Dodging: Your primary goal is survival. Before firing, look at the projectiles being launched by the aliens. Use Left and Right to stay in the "gaps" between falling shots.
2. Align and Fire: Position yourself directly beneath an enemy. Use the Up action to fire. Note that in this game, you usually cannot fire again until your previous shot has either hit a target or left the screen.
games.ALE/Asterix-v5:
Atari Asterix: guide Asterix around the screen, catching desired objects and avoiding the deadly lyres of the bard Cacofonix.
View: top-down with horizontal lanes. Several rows run across the screen; objects scroll horizontally through these rows from one side to the other.
Objective: collect as many positive objects (the clock) as possible while never touching a lyre. There is no terminal goal, the game is score-driven.
Visible elements: the player character (Asterix in the standard variant) drawn as a vertical sprite that occupies one of the horizontal rows at a time; the lyres of Cacofonix, which look like small musical sprites and are lethal on contact; the desirable items (clock) which scroll along the rows.
Controls: Up moves the character one row up; Down moves it one row down. Left and Right move within the current row. There is no Fire / attack button in normal play - the character cannot shoot.
Scoring rules: If you pick up the clock, you will earn scores and the lyres will not come on this row for one round.
Lives / death: The ONLY way to lose a life is to touch a lyre. Falling off the screen edges is not a death - the character is constrained to the playfield. When one life is gone the game ends.
Hidden / non-obvious mechanics: The lyres and the desirable items will not share a row in the same time.
Strategy: prioritize row position over horizontal chase - a single up/down move usually creates the safest collection line; back off when a lyre is approaching your row from either side.
Reward signal in Gym: per-step delta of the raw Atari score (sum of per-object point values).
games.ALE/DemonAttack-v5:
Your goal is to control the laser cannon at the bottom of the screen and destroy waves of demons descending from the sky.
View: Side-on, fixed screen. The horizon line is at the bottom, where your cannon moves left and right. Demons appear higher up on the screen, descending and weaving toward you.
Visible elements: Your laser cannon at the bottom of the screen; flying winged demons, whose sprite appearance changes from wave to wave; descending demon bombs or eggs dropped by demons; and a numeric score at the top of the screen.
Controls: Left and Right move the cannon along the ground.
Scoring rules: Demon point values scale with the wave number. Just destroy as many demons as you can.
Shooting has a cooldown time, so shooting is not guaranteed to respond every action.
You need to move left and right to dodge enemy attacks. If you are hit by an enemy attack, the game ends immediately.
games.ALE/MsPacman-v5:
Your objective is to avoid ghosts while eating pellets in the maze.
View: Top-down 2D maze that fills almost the entire screen. The score and life icons sit on a HUD row below the maze.
Visible elements: Ms. Pac-Man, the player character, is a yellow circle with a bow. There are four ghosts named Blinky, Pinky, Inky, and Sue. Blinky is red, Pinky is pink, Inky is cyan, and Sue is orange. Small dots fill the maze corridors. Four large flashing energizers are located in the corners. A moving bonus fruit bounces through the maze rather than sitting still in a fixed spot. Warp tunnels on the sides of the maze wrap horizontally. The score and remaining lives are shown on the HUD.
Eating a Power Pellet temporarily turns the ghosts blue. At this time, Ms. Pac-Man can eat the ghosts for points. Ghosts that are eaten are reduced to eyes and return to the central box to regenerate. Before the Power Pellet effect ends, the ghosts usually flash and then return to their normal state.
Once you are caught by the ghost, the game will be over.
Scoring rule: Each small dot is worth 10 points. Each large energizer is worth 50 points. After eating an energizer, the ghosts turn dark blue and become edible for a few seconds. The first ghost eaten during a single energizer is worth 200 points, the second is worth 400, the third is worth 800, and the fourth is worth 1600. The chain resets the next time you grab an energizer. Two bonus fruits appear per maze. Published point values for Ms. Pac-Man fruits are commonly cited as Cherry 100.
Fruits appear periodically in the maze, eating them provides extra points.
games.ALE/Alien-v5:
Game Description
This is a retro-style maze-chase game where the player controls a character.
Core Mechanics & Rules
- The Player: You control the purple figure. Movement is grid-based and directed by directional actions (Left, Right, Up, Down).
- The Enemies: Other figures (pink, yellow, green, etc.) roam the maze.
- The Eggs (White Dots): These are the primary scoring objects.
  - Visibility: While white dots are clearly visible on the left side of the screen, they also exist on the right side of the screen but are transparent (invisible). You must navigate the right side of the maze even if it appears empty to collect these hidden points.
- The Shining Star (Power-up Pulsar): Located at the top-center of the maze.
  - Transparency Effect: When you enter the neighborhood of the star, your character becomes transparent. You remain transparent until you either move away from the star or collect it.
  - Invincibility: Collecting the star grants you a short period of invincibility, allowing you to safely pass through or eliminate enemies.
- Scoring: Collecting dots increases your score.
- Failure Condition: Getting caught by or colliding with an enemy leads to an immediate game over.
- Victory Condition: Collecting 25 more eggs triggers Victory state.
Step-by-Step Guidance & Strategy
1. Clear the Visible Area First: Start on the left side of the screen to collect the visible white dots. This allows you to build a baseline score while tracking enemy movements.
2. Navigate the "Empty" Right Side: Do not ignore the right side of the maze. Because the eggs there are transparent, move through those corridors systematically to ensure you are maximizing your score.
3. Manage Enemy Aggression: Watch the enemies carefully. Use the maze's walls to create distance. If an enemy is blocking your path, wait for them to move or find an alternative route.
4. The Pulsar Maneuver: If an enemy is chasing you near the top, head toward the star. The transparency can be used to confuse your tracking of the character, but the invincibility upon collection will guarantee your safety.
games.ALE/Phoenix-v5:
Atari Phoenix: a fixed-shooter in the Galaxian/Space Invaders family. You pilot a small ship at the bottom of the screen and shoot waves of bird-like enemies above you.
Objective: survive five repeating stages of attackers, culminating in a fight against an alien mothership, and rack up points before you run out of ships.
View: side-on, fixed screen. Your ship slides horizontally at the bottom and fires straight up. Enemies descend from the top.
Visible elements: your ship sprite; flocks of small phoenix birds in early waves; large phoenix birds that hatch from eggs in middle waves; the alien mothership / fortress in the final wave; enemy bombs falling from above; the score and a row of remaining ships (lives) on the HUD.
Controls: move left and right at the bottom of the playfield, fire straight up, and activate a temporary force-field shield. In some control schemes the shield is bound to a downward joystick pull. The shield lasts about 1.5 seconds and then takes roughly 3.5 seconds to recharge before you can use it again; while shielded you cannot move but you can still shoot.
Scoring (from the Atari 2600 manual): small phoenixes in horizontal flight are 20 points each. Small phoenixes shot while actively swooping at you are 80 points each. Large phoenixes (waves 3-4) score between 100 and 500 points depending on how close they are when you kill them; merely clipping a wing scores 20 and the wing regenerates after a moment. The alien spaceship in wave 5 is worth 1,000 to 4,000 points on the first round depending on its altitude when killed, and that ceiling increases by 1,000 each loop up to 9,000.
Lives and death: you typically start with five ships. You lose a ship when an enemy bird, the mothership, or an enemy bomb hits you without a shield active. Colliding with a swooping bird also kills you. Game over when all ships are gone.
Wave structure: Waves 1-2 are formations of small phoenixes that strafe horizontally then dive. Waves 3-4 are larger phoenixes that hatch from drifting eggs (one shot pops an egg, but a hatched phoenix needs a body hit because wings regrow). Wave 5 is the fortress/mothership: a large structure with a rotating shield band you must shoot through to expose and kill the pilot, while small phoenixes harass you. After wave 5 the cycle restarts harder.
Special mechanics: the shield cooldown is invisible but strict, so spamming the shield will leave you unprotected at the worst moment. Wings on big phoenixes regenerate, so always go for the body.
Strategy: lead diving birds rather than chasing them; conserve the shield for unavoidable swoops; in the fortress wave aim through the slit in the rotating shield band and stay mobile to dodge falling bombs.
Reward signal in Gym: per-step score delta from the underlying ALE score. No documented shaping in ALE/Gymnasium.
games.ALE/RoadRunner-v5:
Game Description
This is a retro-style arcade evasion game. The player controls a fast-running bird (the protagonist) on a four-lane desert highway.
Core Mechanics & Rules
- The Protagonist: A purple/blue character running along a highway.
- The Pursuer: A brown character that follows the player from the right side of the screen.
- Obstacles: Trucks travel along the lanes.
- Scoring (Bird Seed): As the player runs, piles of bird seed appear on the road (often heralded by a "BIRD SEED" sign). Collecting the first pile of bird seed gives 100 points. Successive collectings without a miss gives more points with the stride of 100, while a miss will reset this mechanism.
- Controls:
  - Left: Slows the character down or moves them toward the left side of the screen.
  - Up / Down: Shifts the character between the four highway lanes.
  - Up+Left / Down+Left: Diagonal movement used for rapid lane switching while decelerating.
- Failure Condition 1: If the pursuer catches the protagonist, the game ends immediately.
- Failure Condition 2: Colliding with a truck results in failure and ends the game.
- Success Condition: Getting 1100 points by collecting the piles of bird seed.
Guidance & Strategy
1. Collecting Bird Seed: When the "BIRD SEED" sign appears, scan all four lanes. Use diagonal movements (like Down+Left) to quickly align with the seed piles. Each pile collected increases your score and is vital for progression.
2. Truck Awareness: When the "CARS AHEAD" sign appears, prioritize safety over points. Trucks occupy an entire lane and move quickly; ensure you are in a clear lane well before the truck enters the frame.
games.highway-v0:
Game Description
This is a high-stakes highway driving simulation game where the player controls a green car navigating through a multi-lane highway filled with light blue traffic.
Core Mechanics & Rules
- The Scoring System (Risk vs. Reward):
  - The game rewards aggressive driving. The faster your vehicle travels, the higher the point, which ranges from 0 to 1 for each step, you receive.
- Controls:
  - Faster: Increases your speed, moving you forward more quickly relative to other cars.
  - Slower: Decreases your speed, allowing you to hang back or wait for gaps in traffic to open.
  - Left / Right: Allows you to switch between the highway lanes to avoid slower-moving cars.
  - Idle: Maintains your current speed and lane.
- The Failure Condition (Collision):
  - Any contact with the light blue cars results in an immediate failure and ends the game.
- The Victory Condition:
  - Successfully navigating the traffic without crashing and getting 25 accumulated points triggers the "Victory" state.
Step-by-Step Guidance & Strategy
To achieve victory and maximize your score, follow these strategies derived from the gameplay:
1. Active Deceleration: While speed gives rewards, safety is paramount. When traffic becomes dense or a collision seems imminent, do not hesitate to use the "Slower" action. Decelerating gives you more time to react and perform precise lane changes.
2. The "Idle" Maneuver: When you find a clear stretch of road or a safe "pocket" behind a blue car, use "Idle". This maintains your current momentum without needing constant input, allowing you to focus purely on the lane markers.
3. Look Ahead: Do not just watch the car directly in front of you. Scan the far right of the screen to identify which lanes are merging or which cars are traveling slower. This allows you to plan your lane switches several seconds in advance.
games.ALE/Tennis-v5:
Atari Tennis: a singles match against a CPU opponent.
Objective: Survive for as many steps as possible, or defeat the opponent.
View: top-down. You control the upper one of the two players.
The net runs horizontally across the middle of the court.
Movement: you can move up/down/left/right around your half of the court. The opponent moves on its own.
Hitting the ball: you swing automatically when the ball reaches you; positioning is what determines whether you actually contact the ball, and the angle/depth of the return depends on where on your body the ball is when you hit it. There is no separate 'swing' button — Fire is often used to serve.
Serving: when you are the server, press Fire to toss and hit the serve. The ball must clear the net and land in the opponent's service box. However, the system has basically pre-set your state after serving, so you only need to focus on receiving the ball.
Scoring: points are awarded based on the number of steps you survive. If the maximum truncation steps are reached or the opponent is defeated, you get full points.
Strategy: anticipate the speed and direction of the ball by comparing the ball's state between consecutive frames, move to intercept the ball early, aim near the baseline, and try to pull the opponent out of position.
games.ALE/ChopperCommand-v5:
Atari Chopper Command: a horizontal shooter where you fly a military helicopter over a desert to defend a convoy of trucks from enemy aircraft.
Objective: destroy all enemy helicopters and jets in each wave while keeping the friendly trucks alive.
View: side-on, horizontally scrolling with wraparound. The desert and trucks scroll below you; the sky above contains enemy aircraft.
Visible elements: your helicopter sprite; enemy helicopters and faster enemy jets; a convoy of friendly trucks driving along the ground; enemy missiles which split into two trajectories (one going up, one going down) after being fired; the score; and at the bottom of the screen the long-range scanner radar that shows all aircraft positions including those off-screen.
Controls: tilt left and right to fly horizontally, and press fire to shoot. There are key combinations available, allowing you to move and shoot at the same time. Ammunition is unlimited.
Scoring: 10 points for killing an enemy, with a maximum score of 100 points. Being killed by an enemy will truncate your score to below 50.
Death: you die when you are hit by an enemy bullet, collide with an enemy aircraft, or fly into one of your own trucks (which also destroys the truck). Note that enemy missiles cannot be shot down, only dodged.
Special mechanics: the radar reveals threats long before they appear on screen, so reading it is essential. Friendly trucks are both the win condition (they determine the wave bonus) and a collision hazard.
Strategy: prioritize killing aircraft over chasing trucks. Be careful to maintain a certain distance from enemies and avoid being at a 45-degree angle from them, otherwise you are easily hit.
games.ALE/Berzerk-v5:
Atari Berzerk: a top-down maze shooter. You play a human trapped in a series of robot-filled rooms with electrified walls.
Objective: shoot as many robots as possible and escape each room.
View: top-down. Each room is a single screen made of corridors and pillars whose walls are deadly to touch.
Visible elements: your humanoid; multiple colored robots; their laser bullets; the electrified maze walls themselves; exits on each side; score and remaining-lives display on the HUD.
Controls: you can move up, down, left, right or shoot, or you can also choose various key combinations.
Scoring: points are awarded for killing enemies, with a maximum score achieved by killing 12 enemies, but dying will truncate your score to below 50.
Death: you die if you are hit by a robot's laser or if you touch the electrified maze wall. Robots can also kill each other with friendly fire if you bait them into the line of fire.
Strategy: never stand still; clear a path to the far exit while shooting robots in passing; bait robots into walls or each other for free kills.
games.ALE/BattleZone-v5:
Your objective is to control your tank and destroy enemy automatons on the battlefield.
View: The Atari 2600 port uses a first-person periscope view from inside the tank, supplemented by a radar. You do not see your own tank as a third-person sprite during play. Geometric obstacles, such as cubes and pyramids, sit on the battlefield.
Visible elements: The periscope frame with a crosshair; enemy vehicles currently visible ahead of you; geometric solid obstacles that block movement and shots; a radar at the top center showing enemy positions as white blips relative to you, with two lines indicating your field-of-view cone; and the score and remaining tanks on the HUD.
Your main screen only shows what is directly in front of your tank, so you need to use the radar at the top of the screen to locate enemies. Enemy units appear as blips on the radar. Turn your tank until an enemy is within your field of view, then aim and fire your turret gun.
You will encounter several types of enemies. Tanks are the most common enemies and move slightly slower than your tank. Supertanks look similar to regular tanks but move faster. Fighters appear in front of you, zigzag toward your tank, and fire when they get close. Flying saucers do not shoot, but they are difficult to hit and can distract you.
You cannot fire another shot until your current shell either hits an enemy or disappears from the screen.
If you get hit by enemy fire, the game will be over.
Strategy 1: Enemies can still fire at you even when they are outside your visible screen. Keep watching the radar and keep moving after firing.
Strategy 2: If you see an enemy fire, turn and move your tank diagonally at about a 45-degree angle away from the direction the shot is coming from. This makes it easier to dodge the projectile.
games.ALE/Riverraid-v5:
Your objective is to control your jet, fly down the river, and score as many points as possible by destroying enemy vehicles, fuel depots, and bridges. 
View: Top-down vertical scroll. The river scrolls past you from top to bottom. Your jet stays near the bottom of the screen, and you can move it left and right within the river while also adjusting forward and backward speed.
Visible elements: Your jet; enemy helicopters; enemy tankers, which are boats; enemy jets; gun positions; fuel depots on the river; bridges that separate river sections; the riverbanks themselves; a fuel gauge at the bottom of the screen; the score; and your remaining reserve jets.
The river is constantly scrolling forward. You can move left and right to steer your jet, and you can speed up or slow down to control your movement. Avoid crashing into the riverbanks, islands, bridges, and enemy objects.
You will encounter different enemy targets, including tankers, helicopters, jets, and bridges. Shooting these targets gives you points.
Scoring: According to the Atari 2600 manual, tankers are worth 30 points, helicopters are worth 60 points, fuel depots are worth 80 points, jets are worth 100 points, and bridges are worth 500 points 
Your game will be over if you crash into the riverbank, hit an enemy object or hit a bridge.
Strategy: Slow down when flying through areas with many enemy targets. This helps you turn more precisely and attack enemies more effectively.
games.ALE/Turmoil-v5:
Your objective is to move up and down the center alley, survive as long as possible, and destroy enemies.
View: Side-on full screen. Seven horizontal alleys are stacked vertically. A central vertical alley lets you change rows. Enemies enter from either the left or the right end of each alley and travel across.
Visible elements: Your ship in one of the seven alleys; multiple enemy types entering from both ends; the central vertical alley you use to switch rows; bonus prize icons that flash at one end of an alley; and the score and remaining ships on the HUD.
Enemy types: According to the Atari 2600 manual, there are five categories of attackers. Standard enemy ships of several visual types travel through alleys and destroy you on contact. Faster enemy variants are worth more points than slower ones. Arrows must be destroyed before they reach the far side, because any arrow that crosses an alley turns into a Tank. Tanks can only be destroyed by shooting them from behind; shooting a tank from the front only pushes it backward. A Ghost Ship is indestructible and must be avoided.
Sometimes a flashing orb appears at the far end of a tunnel after an enemy is destroyed. You can move down the tunnel to collect it for bonus points, but if you wait too long, it turns into a fast-moving missile that can destroy you.
If you hit an enemy object, the game will be over.
games.ALE/Trondead-v5:
Your objective is to survive as long as possible and use the disc to defeat the enemy warriors. 
You control a character named TRON, using a disc to knock down enemies while dodging their discs.
View: Top-down. The arena is a single room with four doors, one on each side, through which enemies and TRON himself can enter, exit, or warp.
Visible elements: TRON in the center of the arena, holding a disc or having just thrown one; up to three computer warriors on screen at once, color-coded by point value; the disc itself, which appears as a moving line while in flight and as a square when floating before recall; the four doors, which may be open, jammed open, or closed; the score; and a visible strength meter that decreases as TRON gets hurt.
You can move TRON in eight directions. Press the fire button to throw TRON’s disc in the direction you are currently aiming. TRON’s disc can only damage enemies while it is traveling away from him, and it has no attack effect on the return path. No matter where you are, the disc will automatically return to TRON’s hand.
If you get hit by enemy discs, the game will be over.
Strategy 1: Keep TRON moving at all times. Standing still makes it much easier for enemy warriors to hit you with their discs.
Strategy 2: Avoid getting trapped in corners. Corners limit your movement and make it harder to dodge incoming discs.
games.aFlappyBird-v1:
Game Description
This is a 2D side-scrolling arcade game. The player controls a small orange bird attempting to navigate through a series of narrow openings between green pipes.
Core Mechanics & Rules
- The Protagonist: A bird that is constantly affected by gravity.
- Controls:
  - Flap: Each "Flap" action provides a quick upward boost to the bird’s altitude.
  - NOOP (No Operation): When no action is taken, the bird descends toward the ground due to gravity.
- The Obstacles: Tall green pipes with varying heights appear from the right side of the screen. Each set of pipes has a small gap that the bird must fly through.
- Failure Condition (Critical Rule): Colliding with any part of a green pipe or ground results in an immediate failure and ends the game.
- Victory Condition: Successfully passing through 3 pipes triggers the "Victory" state.
Step-by-Step Guidance & Strategy
To achieve victory, follow these strategic tips based on the gameplay sequence:
1. Master the Rhythm: The key to success is timing your "Flap" actions. Do not spam the flap button; instead, use single flaps to maintain a steady height.
2. Manage the Descent: Use the NOOP action to let the bird fall naturally when approaching a lower gap. Understanding how fast the bird falls is crucial for positioning it at the mouth of the gap.
3. Positioning for the Gap: Aim for the center or slightly below the center of the gap. This gives you the maximum room for error if you need to flap quickly to avoid the bottom pipe or drop to avoid the top one.
4. Focus on the Next Pipe: As soon as you clear one obstacle, look at the height of the incoming pipes. If the gap is high, start flapping immediately. If the gap is low, use NOOP to descend into position.
games.tetris_gymnasium/Tetris:
Game Description
This is a classic Tetris-style block-dropping puzzle. The player must manipulate various geometric shapes (Tetrominoes) as they fall into a vertical well.
Core Mechanics & Rules
- The Well: The main gameplay area where blocks are stacked.
- Tetrominoes: Blocks come in various shapes and colors.
- The Preview Pane: To the right of the well, a gray area displays the sequence of upcoming blocks, allowing the player to plan their moves in advance.
- Clearing: Once a solid horizontal line is formed, it will be cleared.
- Controls:
  - Left / Right: Move the falling block horizontally across the columns.
  - Clockwise: Rotate the block 90 degrees to change its orientation.
  - Drop: Instantly accelerate the block to the bottom of the stack (Hard Drop).
- Failure Condition: If the stack of blocks reaches the very top of the well, the game ends immediately in failure.
- Victory Condition: Successfully clearing 2 lines triggers the "Victory" state.
Step-by-Step Guidance & Strategy
To succeed and reach the "Victory" state, follow the strategic patterns:
1. Analyze the Preview: Always look at the blocks in the top-right corner. Knowing that a "Line" or "Square" is coming next allows you to leave appropriate gaps or flat surfaces.
2. Rotation Mastery: Use the Clockwise action to fit blocks into tight spaces.
3. Horizontal Precision: Use Left and Right to align blocks perfectly with existing gaps. Avoid leaving "holes" (empty spaces covered by a block), as these are difficult to fill later.
4. Strategic Dropping: Use the Drop action when you are certain the block is perfectly aligned to keep the game moving quickly.
games.procgen_:procgen-bigfish-v0:
Game Description
This is an underwater survival and growth game where the player controls a small green fish navigating a deep blue ocean environment. The sea is filled with various other fish of different colors and sizes.
Core Mechanics & Rules
- The Protagonist: You control a small green fish.
- The Environment: A 2D underwater space where other fish swim across the screen at varying speeds and depths.
- Controls:
  - Up / Down: Used to change your vertical depth in the water.
  - Left / Right: Used to swim horizontally or adjust your speed relative to the scrolling environment.
  - NOOP (No Operation): Allows the fish to glide or maintain its current position without active input.
- Failure Condition: Size is the determining factor for survival. Getting eaten by any fish larger than yourself results in an immediate failure and ends the game.
- Victory Condition: Eating 4 smaller fished results in a success.
Guidance & Strategy
To achieve victory and avoid the "Game Over" screen, follow these strategic tips:
1. Lane Discipline: Treat the vertical space as a series of lanes. If you see a large fish approaching at your current depth, use the Up or Down actions to move to a different "lane" well before they reach you.
2. Identify Safe Zones: Look for gaps in the traffic of larger fish. The safest place is usually behind a large fish that has already passed your horizontal position.
games.procgen_:procgen-bossfight-v0:
Game Description
This is a space-themed, boss-battle-style shooting game. The player controls a small spacecraft at the bottom of the screen, facing a massive boss.
Core Mechanics & Rules
- Movement: The player can move in any direction (Up, Down, Left, Right) to dodge obstacles and line up attacks.
- Combat: Use the Shoot action to fire projectiles.
- The Boss & The Shield: The boss attacks with radial and targeted bursts projectiles. It also periodically wears a protective cover (the gray shroud around its head).
- Failure Conditions:
  - Boss Projectiles: Touching any projectile fired by the boss ends the game.
  - Stones (Asteroids): Colliding with the gray drifting stones results in an instant failure.
- Victory Condition: It typically takes 1 to 10 successful hits during a vulnerable window to trigger the "Victory" state, depending on the initial health that the boss has, which varies from config to config.
Guidance & Strategy
To survive the bullet hell and achieve victory, use the following tactical approach:
1. Survival During Shield Phases: When the boss has its protective cover active, your primary focus should be defense.
2. Identify the Vulnerability Window: Watch the boss closely. When the protective cover moves or the boss’s animation changes to expose its "face" or core, it is vulnerable. This is your window to earn points.
3. Position and Burst Fire: Once the cover is gone, move Left or Right to align perfectly with the boss’s center. Rapidly use the Shoot action to continuously land hits before the shield returns.
games.procgen_:procgen-caveflyer-v0:
Game Description
This is a precision-based space navigation game where the player controls a small spacecraft. The game is set within a dark, star-filled cave bounded by a light-gray patterned region. 
Core Mechanics & Rules
- The Ship: A responsive craft that uses thrust-based physics. When moving forward, a flame trail appears behind the engine.
- Controls:
  - Up: Applies thrust, moving the ship forward in the direction it is facing.
  - Left / Right: Adjusts the ship’s orientation and horizontal position within the tunnel.
  - NOOP (No Operation): The ship coasts based on its existing momentum. This is vital for navigating tight spaces where active thrusting might cause a collision.
- Hazards & Failure Conditions:
  - Obstacles: Collision with drifting stones (asteroids) or other ships (enemies/NPCs) results in instant failure.
  - Red Circles: These denote "wrong places" or danger zones. Entering these areas ends the game.
- Victory Condition: Successfully navigating to the end of the cave and passing through the green glowing ring.
Step-by-Step Guidance & Strategy
To achieve victory, follow these tactical principles:
1. Thrust Management: Do not hold the Up action continuously. The ship carries momentum. Use short bursts of thrust to move forward, then switch to NOOP to glide. This allows you more time to make micro-adjustments with Left and Right.
2. Dodge Drifting Stones: Stones often sit in the middle of the path. When approaching a stone, use a diagonal movement pattern (Thrusting while turning) to "slingshot" around it.
3. Manage Enemy Ships: Other ships move in predictable paths; observe their movement and wait for a gap before thrusting past them.
games.procgen_:procgen-dodgeball-v0:
Game Description
This is a top-down tactical action game where the player controls a character navigating a maze-like environment.
Core Mechanics & Rules
- The Protagonist: A character capable of 4-way movement and shooting.
- The Enemies: Hostile characters that patrol the area. They can launch white projectiles (balls) at the player.
- Obstacles: Light gray solid walls that define the path.
- The Target: A square tile that serves as the exit. Reaching this square triggers the "Victory" state.
- Controls:
  - Up / Down / Left / Right: Directional movement through the environment.
  - Shoot: Launches a white ball in the direction the player is facing to defend against enemies.
  - NOOP (No Operation): Standing still to observe patterns or wait for a projectile to pass.
- Failure Conditions:
  - Collision: Touching any wall or an enemy results in an immediate game over.
  - Projectiles: Getting hit by a white ball launched by an enemy ends the game.
- Success Conditions:
  - After successfully defend all the enemies, the initially red square tile will become green; arriving at the green square tile triggers the victory state;
Step-by-Step Guidance & Strategy
To achieve victory, follow these tactical principles:
1. Maintain Distance: Enemies are most dangerous when they have a clear line of sight. Keep your distance and use the horizontal and vertical walls as cover.
games.procgen_:procgen-heist-v0:
Game Description
This is a top-down maze puzzle game where the player controls a small character navigating through a grid-based labyrinth. 
Core Mechanics & Rules
- The Protagonist: A small character that moves one tile at a time.
- Movement: The game uses four-way directional controls: Up, Down, Left, and Right.
- Keys and Locks:
  - The maze contains colored keys (Blue and Green) and colored doors/blocks with keyholes.
  - Matching Rule: You must collect a key of a specific color to pass through a door of the same color.
  - Inventory: Once a key is collected, it appears in the top-right corner of the screen, indicating it is ready for use.
- Victory Condition: Successfully navigating the maze and collecting the Yellow Gem at the end of the path triggers the "Victory" state.
Step-by-Step Guidance & Strategy
To achieve victory, you must follow a specific sequence of collection and unlocking:
1. The game is a logic-based "lock and key" puzzle. Always look for the keys before approaching the doors, and pay attention to the color-coding to ensure you are following the correct path of progression.
games.procgen_:procgen-leaper-v0:
Game Description
This is a classic arcade-style action game where the player controls a green frog.
Core Mechanics & Rules
- The Highway: The first section of the game consists of several lanes of traffic. Cars of various colors travel at different speeds.
- The River: The second section is a blue river with brown circular platforms (logs) drifting horizontally across the screen.
- Movement: The character moves in discrete hops.
  - Up/Down/Left/Right: Directional movement to navigate the environment.
  - NOOP (No Operation): Standing still to wait for a gap in traffic or for a platform to align.
- Physics of the River: While standing on a brown platform in the river, the frog drifts horizontally at the same speed as the platform.
- Failure Conditions:
  - Car Collision: Being hit by any vehicle on the road results in instant failure.
  - Drowning: Stepping into the blue water of the river (falling off a platform) results in instant failure.
- Victory Condition: Successfully landing on the checkered area at the top of the screen triggers the "Victory" state.
Guidance & Strategy
To achieve victory, follow these tactical phases:
1. Phase 1: The Road (Timing and Positioning)
  - Don't just rush forward. Use NOOP to observe the speed of the cars.
  - If a car is approaching, use Left or Right to stay in the gaps between vehicles within a single lane before hopping Up to the next one.
2. Phase 2: The Median (Safe Zone)
  - The area between the road and the river is a safe zone. Stop here (using NOOP) to synchronize your jumps with the moving river platforms.
3. Phase 3: The River (Momentum Management)
  - Identify a brown platform and hop Up onto it.
  - Because the platforms move, you must be prepared to move Left or Right while on a platform to stay centered, or wait for the next platform in the row above to drift into range before hopping Up again.
games.procgen_:procgen-ninja-v0:
Game Description
This is a 2D side-scrolling platformer game where the player controls a small green character.
Core Mechanics & Rules
- The Protagonist: A green character capable of jumping and horizontal movement.
- The Environment: The world consists of solid brick structures and small floating platforms. Below the platforms is a "sea" of bombs.
- Controls:
  - Up: Jump. This allows the character to reach higher platforms or cross gaps.
  - Down: Used for descending or dropping through specific areas.
  - Left / Right: Move the character horizontally.
- Progress Bar: A green vertical bar appears in the bottom-left corner, indicating the height or power of a jump during specific maneuvers.
